And this makes perfect sense, right? So, the Khazar Empire is very ambitious as well. Okay, it sees itself as a great power eventually wants to unite the different tribes of steppe nations and conquer the world. But to do that, it needs its own distinct identity. So it's not going to convert to Christianity or Islam.

At the same time, their intimate contact with Byzantium and the Caliphate had taught the Khazars that their primitive shamanism was not only barbaric and outdated compared to the great monotheistic creeds but also unable to confer on the leadership the spiritual and legal authority which the rulers of the two theocratic world powers enjoyed. Yet, conversion to either creed would have meant submission, the end of independence, and thus would have defeated its purpose.

What could have been more logical than to embrace a third creed which was uncommitted towards either of the two yet represented the venerable foundation of both?
